findings.where: The full-width blue band straight under the hero, 'Get Mark's briefings on PPP reform' and its white 'Subscribe' button (desktop second screen; phone, right after the hero's action)
findings.fault: The Subscribe button is a dead action. It only jumps to #subscribe on the same page, and the page has no sign-up form, field or list anywhere. It also takes away the hero's one action: a white button on a full field of house blue is the strongest action on the page, stronger than 'Write to me directly'. On a phone it is the next thing seen after the address. So the page has two primary actions, and the louder one does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who taps Subscribe to follow Mark's work and gets nothing. Mark and the founder would object too: the brief's one action is to reach Mark directly, and this band pulls attention from it to an offer that does not exist.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lifted blue card at the end of the article: 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge · Lecture · 23 April 2026' with a download arrow and 'PDF'
findings.fault: The card promises a PDF download with its arrow icon and 'PDF' label, but its link goes to #article, an anchor on this same page. Clicking it downloads nothing and opens no document, so it is a false affordance for the very action it names.
findings.who_objects: A reader who wants the lecture paper. The research calls the PDF list 'the product' for this audience, so a download that silently fails costs the depth the page is meant to offer.

findings.where: Hero, the top bar: 'Mark M. Moseley' and the MMM Infra mark, with no other navigation (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The first screen has no navigation: no way to his articles, his background or his talks. The only bar item that does anything is the logo, which links back to the top. The brief's first screen asks for a nav, and the palette's own notes give 'nav links' a colour, but none appear on the page.
findings.who_objects: A visitor from a multilateral bank who wants to check Mark's record or read his writing before writing to him. They can't go anywhere from the homepage except the email address.

findings.where: Hero, top bar: the name 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the linked logo
findings.fault: The name sits in the bar where a home link goes, set off by its divider and drawing its own box, but it is static. The logo next to it is a link, so the pair reads as one home link and only half of it works.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks the name to get home, as on most personal sites, and finds it does nothing. A small surprise, since the logo beside it works.

findings.where: Article specimen, the blue numbers on the three-item list; also the blue tracked 'PALETTE' label over the palette
findings.fault: Static text takes the link blue, which the page reserves for links. Its own note under the article says 'Grey for reading, blue only where something can be clicked.' The list numbers and the 'PALETTE' label are blue and do nothing, so blue on this page means two different things.
findings.who_objects: A reader who takes the blue numbers for links, as the page has taught. Angélique would also be left with a rule the template itself breaks when she adds lists to articles.
